blocking.issue: The QUIC-loss bullet adds a new case: a Hot Reload that replaces the UDP socket loses in-flight QUIC connections. It cites OQ-system-overview-18 for this case, but that question covers only upgrades. The owning document promises that Hot Reload drops no in-flight request, and that when a listener is removed, its connections finish. So the ADR states an exception to the owning document's Hot Reload guarantee without routing it anywhere. No Open question covers it, and the 'Proposed owning-document amendments' bullet for Data plane does not mention it either. The ADR also misattributes the exception to an Open question about a different event. The technical claim is plausible: a new socket on the same UDP port under SO_REUSEPORT re-hashes existing flows. That is why the case has to be recorded, not silently attached to the upgrade question.
blocking.evidence: Line 92: "- Bad, because in-flight QUIC connections on UDP 8443 are lost at a Zero-Downtime Upgrade, or when a Hot Reload replaces the UDP socket, while TCP connections Drain ([ADR-0015](0015-zero-downtime-upgrades-so-reuseport.md), OQ-system-overview-18)." System overview, Open questions: "| OQ-system-overview-18 | Can upgrades keep in-flight QUIC connections? | Accept loss (current); connection-ID steering | data-plane | No |". Foundation pack 8.4: "loses in-flight QUIC connections on a binary upgrade (OQ-system-overview-18)". Data plane, Summary: "configuration snapshot swaps during Hot Reload that drop no in-flight request". Data plane, Why no in-flight request is dropped: "3. **Listeners stay bound.** An added listener opens before the swap; a removed one stops accepting after it while its connections finish." Foundation pack glossary, Hot Reload: "in-flight requests keep their snapshot."
blocking.fix: Change line 92 to: "- Bad, because in-flight QUIC connections on UDP 8443 are lost at a Zero-Downtime Upgrade ([ADR-0015](0015-zero-downtime-upgrades-so-reuseport.md), OQ-system-overview-18) and when a Hot Reload replaces an `http3` socket, a case Data plane does not yet record, while TCP connections Drain." In the Data plane bullet under 'Proposed owning-document amendments', after "`StrictMaxConcurrentRequests` false in Upstream layer," insert: "the QUIC loss when a Hot Reload replaces an `http3` socket, with an Open question on reusing it,". The fix adds about 22 words, and the body is at about 1,494 of 1,500. To stay under the maximum without cutting any text that closed an earlier finding, cut two things. First, the duplicate "which KrakenD lacks ([source](https://www.krakend.io/features/))" in the Context question on line 21, which the TCP-only option (line 37) and its Bad bullet (line 128) already cite; this saves about 4 words. Second, line 107's "so no extra module serves 8080", about 6 words. Then shorten the fasthttp Bad bullet on line 118 to "Bad, because connect-go needs `net/http` handlers ([source](https://github.com/connectrpc/connect-go/blob/main/README.md)), so a Node would run two server stacks.", saving about 8 words, since the Deadlines row already sources the SSE and ResponseController dependency. If that is still not enough, drop "in floor and release jobs" on line 99 only after checking with L1.

non_blocking.section: Decision outcome, FIPS builds row (line 49) and More information (line 138)
non_blocking.suggestion: `ruralz_fips` is a feature build tag. Repository layout and conventions currently bans feature tags: "| Build constraints | Platform, Go version and `goexperiment` constraints ... No feature tags (P1) |". The ADR sends this to an amendment ('SHOULD admit `ruralz_fips` as the one feature build tag'), which is acceptable because Repository layout is neither the owning document nor a depends_on document. The amendment bullet should still say plainly that the rule it changes is "No feature tags (P1)", so the owner of that document sees the conflict.

Data plane, Upstream layer says "HTTP/2 Upstreams honor server limits through `HTTP2Config.StrictMaxConcurrentRequests`". The natural reading is that the field is set to true. The ADR pins it false and justifies the choice: `maxConnections` and `maxPendingRequests` bound the queueing, so nothing waits unseen inside `http.Transport`. The proposed amendment ('`StrictMaxConcurrentRequests` false in Upstream layer') covers this. Name the sentence it replaces, so the Data plane owner treats it as a correction and not an addition.

"within the 592 KiB per-connection budget (hypothesis)" relies on a Data plane figure that is made up entirely of HTTP/2 and TLS terms ("header ceiling, HTTP/2 receive buffer, frame buffer ..."). L1-5 covers the feasibility problem. From the consistency side, the HTTP/3 row should cite the figure as the target the new Bounded resources rows must meet, not as an existing budget that QUIC already fits.

non_blocking.section: Decision outcome, FIPS builds row (line 49) and Confirmation, FIPS job (line 100)
non_blocking.suggestion: "never binds UDP 8443" names only the default port. The Configuration model makes `port` a required field on each listener, and HTTP/3 uses "UDP on the `https` port". Write "never binds UDP for an `https` listener" so a FIPS Node with `port: 443` is covered too.

The Configuration model's Gateway section says "`http3: true` is `Planned (M3)` and off in FIPS builds." That sentence can be read as the field being silently ignored, which the ADR rules out under pack section 8.1. Extend the amendment so it also rewords that sentence to "refused on FIPS Nodes (RZ-CFG code under OQ-tech-stack-and-libraries-9)".

The verifier shows WARN lines, not FAIL lines. The roadmap has no M5 item for the FIPS `http3: true` refusal, no M1 item matching the PB-8 bullet, and no M3 item matching the standard-library HTTP/3 Bad bullet. For line 123, removing the Planned tag from the rejected option's Bad bullet ("leaving the HTTP/3 work without a library") clears the warning without losing meaning. The other two warnings need roadmap entries, which are outside this document.

Still true after the revision: every HTTP, HTTP/2 and quic-go URL in Considered options is in `docs/_meta/research/go-libraries-runtime.md` or `tooling-and-licenses.md`, and `go-libraries-protocols.md` backs only the `ResponseController` link. The manifest entry should list go-libraries-runtime.md.

foundation_amendments: Foundation pack section 8.4 and System overview OQ-system-overview-18 record the QUIC connection loss only for a binary upgrade. The ADR shows that a Hot Reload that replaces an `https` listener with `http3: true` loses in-flight QUIC connections too, which conflicts with the Hot Reload glossary entry ('in-flight requests keep their snapshot') and Data plane's 'drop no in-flight request'. Widen OQ-system-overview-18 to 'Can upgrades and listener-replacing Hot Reloads keep in-flight QUIC connections?', or have Data plane add its own Open question, and change the section 8.4 sentence to match.

Carried forward and still open: foundation pack section 1 (FIPS build row: 'the same features and license as the default build') and vision P1 ('one feature set in every public build, including the FIPS build') should name the HTTP/3 exception that section 8.4 creates while OQ-tech-stack-and-libraries-9 is open, as ADR-0001, ADR-0009 and the market landscape document (OQ-market-landscape-and-table-stakes-8) already note.
